A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOMIE/PCR work and are readable, including figures, tables and equations. The supplied v3 ends after its references; v4 includes supplementary Appendices A–E. The format and title changes do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original composed-retrieval, simple-retrieval and tile-classification results, component and fusion ablations, and embedding-space analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports original retrieval comparisons, evaluations across six adapted backbones, component and prompt ablations, and qualitative embedding analyses.

M1.justification: The reported visual backbone changes from the Qwen2.5-associated ViT with window attention in v3 Section 3.2 to SigLIP-2 in v4 Section 3.3. The central two-stage adaptation, InfoNCE objective, filtering, curriculum, stain processing and EOL embedding extraction remain. Expanded video and prompt descriptions largely document existing capabilities.

E1.justification: v4 adds the full NLI corpus to training and removes Pubmedset retrieval and all nine tile-classification datasets from reported evaluation. The composed tasks and remaining simple-retrieval datasets retain their coverage and sample counts. Appendix C describes classification inference but does not restore classification evaluations.

E2.justification: v4 Tables 2–3 add Qwen3-VL-2B, Qwen3-VL-8B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Lingshu-7B and PathoR1-7B. Table 2 also evaluates reciprocal rank fusion for all eleven dual-encoder baselines alongside retained vector addition. E5-V, LamRA and GME remain the same comparators despite added size suffixes.

E3.justification: The reported stage-one learning rate changes from 4e-5 to 2e-4. Main evaluations shift from Qwen2.5-VL-7B to Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, with additional backbone configurations and inference-prompt controls. GPT-5 curation is redescribed as strict extraction/formatting, although Appendix E retains generation language; benchmark regeneration is not established.

E4.justification: v4 adds six-backbone generality tests and No Prompt/No One Word robustness ablations. Component ablations now report task-specific retrieval results on Qwen3-VL-8B rather than composed/simple/classification averages. v3's separate simple-add versus prompt-guided fusion ablation disappears. The qualitative examples and modality-gap analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The bootstrap procedure concerns data filtering, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main HOMIE results are replaced: multi-image Bookset R@1 is 78.5 in v3, versus 75.2 and 79.8 for v4's Qwen3 2B and 8B variants. These are different configurations, not demonstrated same-setting gains. v4 adds extensive comparator, backbone and ablation results and removes Pubmedset, classification and fusion-ablation results. Shared baseline rows and modality-gap values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The PCR similarity-ranking formulation and InfoNCE mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs. v4's causal-attention and EOL discussion adds conceptual explanation rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: v4 elevates adaptation of any generative MLLM and a lightweight 2B model outperforming specialized 7B models into central claims. It explicitly organizes the contribution around architectural, task and domain mismatches. v3 emphasizes the public-data, two-stage omni-modal system without equivalent backbone-generality or parameter-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of domain-prior synergy, model scaling and learned prompt robustness. Appendix B introduces limitations concerning real clinical queries, modality coverage and deployment resources. The Pubmedset-overlap explanation and classification-transfer interpretation disappear. Its claimed consistent scaling is qualified by Table 4, where some scores decrease from 2B to 8B.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the filtering threshold 0.1, LoRA ranks and scaling factors, scheduler and warmup, BF16, FlashAttention-2 and DeepSpeed settings. Appendices add inference prompts, dataset-selection details, exact curation prompts and deployment memory/latency information. A project-page link is added; the PDFs alone do not verify its resources.

R1.justification: The related-work section largely retains its pathology dual-encoder versus general embedding framing. v4 adds references supporting Qwen3, SigLIP-2, positional encoding, EOL, NLI training and medical MLLMs, while removing classification-dataset and some contextual references. Positioning now more explicitly addresses specialized generative medical models.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten around model generality and three mismatches. v4 adds an existing-model analysis subsection and five supplementary sections, merges qualitative and embedding-visualization discussion, and changes the title terminology from omni-modal to multi-modal.

P2.justification: v4 switches to a single-column layout, replaces the opening radar presentation with a mismatch-analysis figure, and moves a revised clinical-workflow graphic to the appendix. The qualitative and UMAP figures are merged. Comparison and ablation tables are substantially restructured, a backbone table is added, and curation prompts become figures.

improvement.justification: The added RRF and pathology-MLLM controls, backbone tests, prompt ablations and reproducibility details strengthen support for the central PCR framework beyond v3. The net gain is limited by removal of Pubmedset, where CONCH led, and classification evidence. Reporting also needs correction: v4 gives the 2B Quilt-VQA R@1 as 34.4 in Table 2 but 33.4 in Table 4, and its uniform-scaling interpretation overstates the results.
